data.name: Emraanun
data.gender_notes: Emraanun is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'imr' which means 'to be a rival', 'to strive', or 'to compete'. Emraanun is the name of Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham) second son, Ismaeel, who was born to Hagar and raised in the desert. The name signifies the one who is a ruler and leader of the believers, and the one who strives and competes in the way of Allah.
data.etymology: Emraanun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the Believers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Emraanun total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Emraanun holds a significant cultural impact in Islamic history as it is the name of Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham) second son, Ismaeel, who is considered a pioneer of faith and perseverance in the face of hardship. Ismaeel's story is one of pure devotion and unwavering faith, as he along with his mother Hagar was abandoned in the desert with no resources but managed to survive with Allah's help. This name serves as a reminder of the strength and resilience of the Muslim community and the power of unwavering faith.

It signifies the one who strives and competes in the path of righteousness, embodying the qualities of courage, determination, and perseverance. This name is a reminder that life is a constant competition between good and evil, and that with unwavering faith and dedication, one can overcome any obstacle and emerge victorious. Additionally, the name Emraanun is a link to the story of Prophet Ismaeel, a model of unwavering faith and devotion, and a reminder of the blessings and rewards that come from remaining steadfast in faith.
